newsitem.title: USA: Gasoline demand rises ahead of holidays.
newsitem.headline: Gasoline demand rises ahead of holidays.

text.p: In keeping with the season, gasoline inventories were drawn down and heating oil stocks built up last week as retailers stocked up for holiday driving and refiners girded for colder weather, analysts said.

Based on inventory estimates from the American Petroleum Institute released Tuesday, analysts said demand for gasoline from U.S. refineries was about 8.4 million barrels a day last week, the second straight week of unseasonally strong demand.

"That's more of a June or an August-type demand number," said Peter Beutel, an energy analyst with Cameron Hanover in Bronxville, New York. "You normally get a tiny increase during the autumn foliage season, but usually less than 150,000 barrels (a day) or so," he said.
Under pressure to boost heating oil supplies in the Northeast, U.S. refineries were running at a frantic 94 percent of capacity, the Washington-based trade group said.

Refiners reported a net 3.83 million barrel draw in gasoline inventories and net 3.59 million barrel build in distillate stocks, which includes heating oil and diesel and jet fuels, the API said in its weekly estimate of inventories on hand at domestic refineries.
The trade group said refiners nationwide had 186.02 million barrels of gasoline and 117.89 million barrels of distillate stocks in primary storage last week.
